## Labels

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `feature request` | A request for a new capability. Triaged onto the board. |
| `roadmap: candidate` | Proposed. Not committed to a release. |
| `roadmap: planned` | Committed, not yet started. |
| `roadmap: shipped` | Delivered in a release. |
| `needs design` | Needs a spec or design pass before implementation. |

`roadmap: candidate` / `planned` / `shipped` mirror the board's Status field. The
label is what makes state visible from inside an issue, where people actually
work; the field is what makes it sortable.

## Board fields

- **Status** — `Todo` / `In Progress` / `Done`
- **Priority** — `P0-Urgent` / `P1-High` / `P2-Medium` / `P3-Low`
- **Area** — `Family tracking` / `Home and inventory` / `Platform`

`Area` exists because the roadmap spans two horizons: the family tracking loop,
and the widening into the home. An item with no area is missing a decision.

## Current direction

This section is the part that changes by hand, and it should only change when the
*shape* of the roadmap changes. Adding an item is an issue plus a board entry, not
an edit here.

### 1. Make the family tracking solid

The tracking loop has to be trustworthy before anything is layered on it, because
the inventory work consumes those same events.

- Per-breast feed timing is captured end to end, so the next feed can say which
  breast was last and how long each was used.
- Milestone-family records (milestones, firsts, routines, medical) are one
  record type with an explicit kind, and categories are a controlled vocabulary
  rather than free text, so they can be reported on.
- Every record type can carry a note.

### 2. Inventory, and the home horizon

Tracked in #11. One inventory covering both family and home use cases, where
stock is consumed by events that are already being recorded, which projects
runout and warns ahead of time.

The first journey is diapers: add a pack, have every recorded diaper change
decrement it, forecast when a size will be outgrown using growth records, and get
notice before running out — through the existing reminders mechanism rather than
a new notification system.

## Conventions for feature requests

- One issue per capability. The issue is the design conversation; the board is
  the schedule.
- Lead with the user journey, not the schema. "Add a pack of diapers, and it
  goes down every time you log a change" tells a reader more than a table
  definition.
- Say which existing subsystem the feature leans on. Most of the roadmap is
  cheaper because something already exists.
- Put the unresolved questions in the issue. An open question is a reason to keep
  something at `roadmap: candidate`, not a reason to guess silently.
